title: Dancing in the street
hookLine: Mira sang and danced with wandering devotees, to her family's shame
tomorrow: if songs carry Mira's name, who actually wrote them?

cards: Someone posts a video of their grandmother dancing at a wedding, and the comments split: iconic, or embarrassing. Mira's in-laws chose embarrassing.
The stories put her in a temple courtyard, bells tied around her ankles, singing to Krishna among wandering holy men, the people a princess of the royal house of Mewar was never supposed to sit with.
Word reaches the palace, and the whispering starts in every room. Their own daughter-in-law, dancing where anyone at all can watch.

teach.h: PAG GHUNGHRU BANDH MIRA NACHI RE.
teach.b: The palace says stop. Her songs answer. One line sung under her name, in her own Rajasthani, goes pag ghunghru bandh Mira nachi re: Mira tied bells on her feet and danced.
In other songs she says she has let go of the family's honor and the world's talk, because her lord is Giridhar Gopal, Krishna, the cowherd who lifted a mountain.

Her family saw a scandal: a royal woman, out in a crowd of wanderers and street singers. Mira saw a love that couldn't stay behind a curtain, any more than a bride could hide her joy on her wedding day.
That love has a name. Mira belongs to bhakti, the Hindu path of loving devotion to God.

teach.h: BHAKTI: LOVE OF GOD, OUT LOUD.
teach.b: Bhakti says love for God isn't only for priests, or for the temple's inner room. It is sung out loud, in your own language, together, and sometimes danced.

You can hear that in the kirtan and bhajans sung in Hindu temples and living rooms, with clapping, drums and voices answering each other, and Mira's songs are still danced to. The stories add one more line she crossed.

teach.h: A TEACHER FROM BELOW HER CASTE.
teach.b: Some tellings give her a teacher, the poet-saint Raidas, a leatherworker by caste, someone her royal family would have looked down on.
Scholars can't confirm that meeting; the songs and stories keep it. Bhakti's point isn't to cause a scene. It is that a love this real doesn't hide.

how: Devotees sing Mira's bhajans in temples and homes, often in a group with clapping, drums and harmonium, and sometimes dance; kirtan is sung as call and response.

games.q: what does “dancing in the street” mean?
o: a street festival for the harvest goddess
Mira singing and dancing for Krishna in public
a royal parade held for a Rajput wedding

games.q: the princess who danced: tap the pairs.
p: a princess who sang and danced for Krishna
Krishna, the cowherd who lifted a mountain
loving devotion to God, out loud
a poet-saint some stories make her teacher

s: Mira kept her devotion private to protect her family's name
the songs and stories say the opposite: she sang and danced in public and let the palace talk.
in bhakti, love for God is sung out loud, together, in your own language
that's why kirtan and bhajans are sung with clapping, drums and answering voices.
historians have confirmed that Raidas was Mira's teacher
some tellings give her that teacher; scholars can't confirm the meeting.

games.q: you're at a friend's family puja. the aunties start a bhajan, and people begin clapping and swaying. you know none of the words. what fits what Mira's story teaches?
o: clap along if you're welcome; in bhakti the shared singing is the devotion itself.
stay still and silent; real devotion is private and shouldn't be watched.
wait it out politely; the singing is entertainment before the real prayers.
games.why: in bhakti, singing together is the worship, not a warm-up. Mira's songs went out loud, among ordinary devotees.

practice: Think of one joy you keep quiet: a song you only sing alone, something you love and shrug off when anyone asks. For two minutes, let it be as big as it really is. Hum it, or let your feet keep time, and don't apologize to anyone.

wordCard.voice: Dancing in the street: Mira's devotion to Krishna, sung and danced in public while her royal family called it shame. In bhakti, love for God goes out loud.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Hindi: devotion, loving attachment to God. The path Mira sang.

carryVoice: Your line: she danced. The palace called it shame, and the songs called it love. See you tomorrow.
